title: Packaging Lab & Media Analysis Fix
summary: Packaging Lab now works from the current video analysis instead of forcing a Radar-first workflow, every generated package is saved into an expandable Package Library, Visuals + Audio is actually wired into the live app, and confusing creator-context/cloud-session states have been rewritten into clear actions.
discord_changes: Packaging Lab now drafts thumbnail, title and opening-hook packages from the current analysis and no longer blocks on the old multi-creator gate.
Every packaging run is now saved as an expandable folder in a persistent Package Library.
Visuals + Audio is now loaded in the live app, with clearer creator-context and cloud reconnect states.
changes: Reframed Packaging Lab around the current analysis: Draft up a thumbnail, title and opening-hook package based off your current analysis.
Removed the frontend requirement that Packaging Lab must first have a verified Radar scan across multiple creators.
Current analysis evidence is now the primary packaging input; saved Radar evidence can still be used as supporting context when available.
Added an expandable Package Library that preserves up to 50 packaging runs and exposes every saved thumbnail direction, title and opening hook.
Added one-click package copying from both the current result and saved package folders.
Wired the existing Visuals + Audio media-analysis scripts into the live loader so the LIVE navigation item now has real functionality behind it.
Rewrote the creator workspace modal so it explains what channel context, niche and competitors are actually used for.
Replaced raw database 401 / JWT issued-at-future messaging with a clear cloud reconnect state and a one-time session refresh attempt.
Clears the stale Sign in required analyser error when the interface already has a synced signed-in session.
Bumped the PWA cache to v0.28.2 so installed copies receive the new media and Packaging Lab code.
why_it_matters: Packaging Lab had strong potential but the old flow made it feel like a compliance screen instead of a creative tool. This release makes it useful immediately after analysing a video, preserves the work so repeated use compounds into a real creative library, and fixes a LIVE media feature that previously was not actually loaded.
